items.alasan: The spoken price (eight hundred dollars) was written into volume, while the spoken volume is twenty-four square feet. Guard rule 3 must hold the field when a price keyword sits within six words of the number.
The row is priced per square metre, but the unit was written as sak (bags of cement). The spoken unit does not match the field's unit, so guard rule 2 must hold it.
The Indonesian decimal comma was read as a thousands separator: 24,5 became 245, ten times too large. Guard rule 4 must normalise comma decimals before comparing.
Delapan puluh ribu (80,000) was written as 800,000: the puluh/ratus reading is off by ten times. Guard rule 4 must normalise Indonesian tens words before comparing.
The row cites turn_4, which belongs to a different session's transcript (sess-en-11 has only turn_1 and turn_2). Guard rule 1 must reject a citation that is not in this session.
The value comes from a partial turn (final=false). Guard rule 1 accepts only final turns, so the field must wait until a final turn states the number.
Spoken "twelve hundred" is 1,200; the document wrote 12,000. The English hundreds idiom must be normalised before the number is compared (guard rule 4).
"Setengah juta" is 500,000; the document wrote 5,000,000, ten times too high. The Indonesian fraction words must be normalised (guard rule 4).
No turn states a volume or a rate: the row's numbers come from nowhere. The guard must ask instead of letting a value appear without a source.
